This rule replaces the earlier ticket-lifespan description:
Whenever someone mints using a referral code, the referrer immediately receives 7 tickets on their NFT:
+4 Small Block Tickets
+3 Big Block Tickets

For the Small Block ($7,200 pool ÷ 8 ÷ $900 draw), draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the previous small block. After the draw, burn and reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.

messages.text:
Recommended route

For true Visa or Mastercard payments, do not use Coinbase Commerce as the fiat processor. Instead, use Stripe with bank settlement (Recommended) for direct card payments that automatically trigger blockchain transactions. This approach provides genuine credit-card payments, requires no cryptocurrency from users, costs less than crypto payments, and offers a familiar checkout flow. Its tradeoffs are mandatory Stripe account verification and a fee of 4.6% + $0.85 per transaction.

Why the cryptocurrency-only route does not fit

Coinbase Commerce is a cryptocurrency gateway, NOT a genuine fiat or credit-card processor. To complete a payment, users must:
1. Already hold cryptocurrency such as USDC, ETH, or BTC
2. Send it from their wallet
3. Accept that credit cards are NOT processed directly

It is therefore unsuitable for true non-crypto users who own no cryptocurrency.

Other fiat on-ramp choices

Third-party gateways can provide actual fiat → crypto conversion:
- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
- Wyre - Fiat gateway that is being sunset
- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

These services offer genuine credit-card payments through ready-made widgets with worldwide coverage. However, their fees are higher at 6-9%, KYC is required, and users still see the crypto conversion.

Coinbase Pay is a separate alternative and differs from Commerce. With Coinbase Pay, users get credit-card payments, OAuth authentication, and fiat → crypto conversion. It benefits from trust in the Coinbase brand and integrates the conversion process, but it requires a Coinbase account and the user must purchase crypto first.

Page Title: About Harbor Quill
Sub-title: A reader-powered release where every recommendation earns rewards.

What is Harbor Quill?
Harbor Quill serves as the live proof of concept for CORA (Community Outreach Response Automation), the first system allowing independent creators to sell unlimited-mint NFT ebooks while paying readers genuine commissions and prize tickets for sharing them.
It launches on Base with my own raw memoir novella, “From Workshop Floor to Fresh Start,” and represents my public mission to help my household's recovery after a six-figure property fraud.

If CORA works here, Harbor Quill will become ArchiveLedger, a community-owned public-good platform for every creator.

Built on Cutting-Edge Technology

- Smart Contracts
Secure, audited Solidity deployed on Base.
- Chainlink VRF

- Aave Connector
Generates yield by depositing prize-pool funds.
- Base Network

- Decentralized
The logic is fully on-chain from launch, initially protected by V1 safeguards and moving toward complete decentralization after battle-testing.

How It Works

Mint Your ebook NFT
Buy the ebook NFT for $30 USD; its mint number becomes your referral code.

Earn Through Referrals
Share the link or mint number. Every mint that uses it immediately earns you $10 USD, with no limits or expiration.

Accumulate Tickets

Win Prizes

Big Block: 9 × $6,000 after every 180,000 sales.
Sales include both mints and secondary transactions.
Chainlink VRF selects winners randomly and fairly.

Claim Your Rewards

Key Features

Automatic Rewards: Smart contracts issue every payment immediately.
Fair Prize Selection: Chainlink VRF supplies true randomness.
Yield Generation: Prize pools generate yield through the Aave connector.
Gamification: Badges and leaderboards keep participation fun and competitive.
Transparency: Every transaction and rule is on-chain and verifiable.
Low Fees: Base provides speed with minimal transaction expenses.

Our Vision
Although Harbor Quill begins with one book, it is intended as only the first step.
The vision is a world where ebooks succeed according to merit, without gatekeepers or Amazon algorithms suppressing independent voices. Unknown and established creators alike should rise because audiences connect with their work—not because they manipulate a platform, have privileged connections, or purchase enough advertising.
Fans should be compensated for word-of-mouth promotion they previously provided for free, while anyone willing to hustle can earn after discovering a worthwhile title to share.

Our goal is a self-sustaining system that serves everyone: artists receive a fair share, fans and affiliates create real income, and communities form direct relationships. In that way, one underdog’s recovery can grow into a decentralized transformation for all creators, driven by aligned incentives rather than hype.

messages.text:
Marcus, I noticed that the landing-page book cover was dramatically expanded. That wasn’t necessary; I preferred it compact, and it only needed to keep every edge visible.

At present it remains expanded and cropped at the margins, so could you please correct both issues?

Do you understand what I mean?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Your point is clear; I understand what you mean.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Now that the book cover is visible edge-to-edge on the landing page, which is great, could you please have it reduced once more?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I just received this email from Transak:

'To complete our KYB review, could you please provide 5 items from the following:
1. We understand that the website will be functional \~Mar 18th 2026. Could you share an annotated screen recording of the checkout and redemption journey showing how the Transak widget will be used on your platform?

Best regards,

Transak Team'

I’m not sure how they expect us to record a feature that has not yet been implemented. Are we still able to produce this?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Okay, thanks

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: That makes sense to me, and yes, we can do it.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’ll record the video next Thursday and share it afterward.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Cool 👍

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: What launch date do you expect for Harbor Quill?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: This is ready to share: it’s a short demo video showing the UX flow for how the Transak widget will be used on our platform.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Would you prefer that we complete the Transak integration during beta, or postpone the work until after launch?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Adding it later seems best. Going live as 'crypto only' is fine, with fiat payments coming in ~3 weeks.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Okay

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: It's now deployed.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Everything is configured and looks good in production. Next, we should begin live testing with real minting in production and observe how the system behaves. We will monitor it closely, fix or adjust anything that appears, and add or modify anything else you think is necessary.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Although this is very cool, I found several bugs.

Two mornings ago, I tried minting 7 times while my wallet held ETH but no USDC. The attempts seemed to fail, yet <http://harborquill.example|harborquill.example> reports that I have minted 8 times.

With the referral field left blank, I am unsure what should have happened to the commission and ticket for mint 8, since they are meant to go to a previously minted NFT owner. This is a recurring edge case I had not considered. The commission and ticket from mint 9 should have been allocated to mint 8, though perhaps that did not happen because the mint itself failed.

There is also a display problem when I open an NFT from the dashboard: the book cover is oversized and cropped on all sides. Possibly because the mint did not complete, I also cannot work out how to view the actual book.

Tomorrow morning, I’ll try another mint using USDC and see what happens.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please send screenshots along with any errors you encounter so I can fix the problems ASAP.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’ll inspect the issue on production and try to fix it there.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The referral field is also accepting '47' as a valid code, even though valid referrals must be NFTs confirmed before checkout to prevent self-referrals. For example, affiliate 87 could persuade me to buy while I am about to mint 864, and I could then enter 864 as the referral code to direct the commission and ticket back to myself.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: USDC mint attempts are failing, although the dashboard is not recording them as purchases.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: These screenshots are excellent, thanks. Please send every issue you encounter, your expected solution, and any suggested tweaks or improvements. Once I have that information, I’ll handle everything properly from my side.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Can you confirm which option you are using and whether it is the Transak option? Please share a screenshot, or record the issue with OBS Studio or the built-in recorder and send the resulting link as well.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I’m not using that option; I’m attempting to mint directly with my wallet.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Okay

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Although I’m tied up with family matters at the moment, I’ll try to send you that screenshare video next Tuesday.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Sure, that's fine.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please document every issue and bug you encounter on production. I’ll then work through them so the user flow operates smoothly.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
The mechanics are the priority because minting is currently failing; the remaining work is mostly aesthetic, including making the book view 25% wider.

The failure might be related to the edge case of where the commission and ticket should go on mint 3.

Other problems include:
\- How can the book be viewed?
\- The dashboard reports that I minted even though I did not
\- A referral code above the current mint number is being shown as rejected

I’ll run another test once I can complete a real mint.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Even with eth and usdc in the wallet, attempting a mint produces the message 'execution reverted'.
